content.title: Reviews Response
content.comment: We thank the reviewers for their time and thoughtful feedback on our paper. After careful consideration, we have decided to withdraw the paper. There is a consensus amongst reviewers that the method and the results are promising and interesting, but more experiments with additional data sets and baselines are needed, in addition to a more clear explanation of the reason for improved robustness. We will make these improvements to the paper and submit to a later venue. We thank the reviewers once again for their comments; we do believe addressing these points will make for a very strong paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper studies the problem of a weak supervision (WS) paradigm where multiple labeling functions (LFs) are used to provide weak labels to an unlabeled dataset. Specifically, the paper proposes to use a VAE-like generative model to model the inputs and weak labels jointly to recover the hidden ground-truth labels. Experimental results show that the proposed model leads to competitive  performance and stronger robustness to the design of LFs compared to existing methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- The paper is overall clearly written and easy to follow.
- The paper is among the first to consider modeling weak labels jointly with the inputs for WS. A VAE-like model is a natural choice and the paper makes contribution to tailoring VAE to WS setting. It is interesting to see this new method’s results compared to existing WS methods.
- Current experimental results, although a bit limited (see below), show that the performance of WS-VAE is promising.

Weaknesses:
- In the Introduction, it is mentioned that “Because the model learns from inputs and weak labels jointly by exploiting its artificial latent space to capture the features distribution, it is substantially more robust to LFs of low accuracy, coverage or high correlation, as well as less reliant on validation ground-truth labels for early stopping during training”. However, it is not clear to me why this is the case. Could the authors elaborate more on this?
- One concern I have about the paper is that the experimental results lack stronger baselines to more properly evaluate the proposed method. Specifically, one way to interpret WS-VAE is that WS-VAE is essentially incorporating the input features when modeling the weak labels and the hidden ground-truth labels. From this angle, it is less surprising that WS-VAE performs better than earlier WS work like Snorkel and FS that model the weak labels $\Lambda$ and true label $y$ independent to the input features. I believe there are more related work that models $\Lambda$, $y$, and $x$ jointly (e.g. [1,2,3]). Comparing to such methods more deeply (both on method design and experimental results) would make the results more convincing. Currently, Weasel is the only included baseline along this line of work, and it has also received little discussion in the paper.
- The SMS dataset is a highly imbalanced dataset. Accuracy doesn’t seem to be a proper evaluation metric. In fact, WRENCH uses F1 for SMS.
- The main results are presented in Figure 3. But it is hard to compare the results precisely in the plots. I’d suggest changing the presentation to tables for easier comparison.
- I appreciate studying the robustness of WS-VAE to LF quality. However, it is not clear to me why the WS-VAE design enjoys stronger robustness compared to other methods. It is only very briefly mentioned in the last part of Sec 3.2. Deeper discussion on this can definitely make the paper stronger.
- Only 4 binary classification datasets are included. Results can be made much more convincing by including more tasks (there are many other datasets available on WRENCH).

[1] Denoising Multi-Source Weak Supervision for Neural Text Classification. Ren et al. 2020.

[2] End-to-End Weak Supervision. Cachay et al. 2021.

[3] Leveraging Instance Features for Label Aggregation in Programmatic Weak Supervision. Zhang et al. 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- Clarity: The paper is overall clearly written.

- Novelty: Applying VAE like model/approach to WS is novel.

- Quality: Paper quality can be improved by discussing more deeply about why the VAE design enjoys advantages over existing baselines, as well as comparing to stronger/more relevant baselines as mentioned above.

- Reproducibility: Experimental details are provided in the paper but there is no code available.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, the main idea of applying VAE-like approach to WS is novel and interesting. However, the current presentation does not motivate the VAE design well. Experimental results can also be much improved with more extensive studies.

content.summary_of_the_paper: Due to the high cost of obtaining a large amount of accurate labels, many weak supervision methods have been proposed to leverage the imperfect labels that are cheaply generated from  simple rule-based functions so as to reduce the necessarily of costly manual labeling significantly. This paper studied how to combine the weak supervision methods with the generative model VAE so as to reduce the requirements of rule-based label functions (LF) on accuracy, coverage, independence assumption etc, increasing the robustness of weak supervision methods w.r.t. label functions. Experiments are conducted on several textual binary classification datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1) The problem studied in this paper is interesting and of practical importance. The idea of combining traditional supervised weak supervision methods with VAE to reduce the reliance on the qualities of LFs is convincing. 

2) The review and introduction to existing weak supervision methods is clear. 


Weakness:
1) My main concern on this paper is the technical novelty. Although the basic idea of combing WS method and generative model is interesting, the proposed combining method is very straightforward, simply adding a decoder branch  to generate the noisy labels and using one latent variable to reflect the binary label information. The whole model is mostly a very small modification to the naive VAE.

2) The experimental results are not convincing. We cannot see how the proposed method outperforms comparable baselines. In Figure 3, we see that the proposed method often perform on par with the most basic baselines. 

3) The model seems to be restricted to the binary case. How to handle classification with categories more than 2?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The presentation of this paper is readable, but there is still large room to be improved. The novelty of the paper is limited.
content.summary_of_the_review: The problem studied in this paper is interning, but the proposed solution looks very straightforward. And the experimental results do not show the performance gains brought by the proposed method when comparing to some most basic baselines.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper focuses on training classifiers with weak supervision. The authors propose a Weak Supervision Variational AutoEncoder (WS-VAE) for solving this problem. The method is tested on several benchmark datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
The authors propose a novel model called WE-VAE. The authors introduce the temperature variable as shown in Equation (3), which is interesting.

WE-VAE outperforms other methods in the experiments.

Weakness
The proposed method is similar to the existing semi-supervised generative model. The authors do not compare the method to such models.
The details about hyper-parameter selection are not provided.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Most sections in this paper are clear. In Section 4.3, the authors need to entail the number of labeled data that is used for validation. The details about hyper-parameter selection are not provided.

My primary concern about the paper is the WS-VAE is very similar to the existing semi-supervised generative model [1]. Both models assume that the data's labels and styles are encoded with separate latent spaces. The authors introduce the temperature variable as shown in Equation (3), which is novel and interesting. However, it is unclear whether the WS-VAE outperforms existing models without comparing them.

References

[1] Kingma, Durk P., Shakir Mohamed, Danilo Jimenez Rezende, and Max Welling. "Semi-supervised learning with deep generative models." Advances in neural information processing systems 27 (2014).
content.summary_of_the_review: The authors proposed WS-VAE, which looks novel. The experimental results will be more convincing if the authors compare WS-VAE with the existing semi-supervised generative model.

content.title: Weak Supervision Variational Auto-Encoder
content.TL;DR: A VAE model with specifically designed components to perform weak supervision. Compared to existing weak supervision methods, it is considerably more robust to labelling functions design.
content.abstract:
Recent advances in weak supervision (WS) techniques allow to mitigate the enormous labelling cost of human data annotation for deep learning by automating it using simple rule-based labelling functions (LFs). However, LFs need to be carefully designed, often requiring expert domain knowledge to be of sufficient accuracy, cover enough data and be independent of each other for existing WS methods to be viable. In addition, weak supervision methods often rely on small amounts of validation data with true labels to fine-tune and select models. 
To tackle these issues, we propose the Weak Supervision Variational Auto-Encoder (WS-VAE), a novel framework that combines unsupervised representation learning and weak labelling to reduce the dependence of WS on expert and manual engineering of LFs. The proposed technique learns from inputs and weak labels jointly and captures the input signals distribution with an artificial latent space, leading to considerably improved robustness to LFs quality. Our extensive empirical evaluation shows that our WS-VAE performs competitively to existing WS on a standard WS benchmark while it is substantially more robust to LF engineering.
